 How Ousmane Dembélé conquered the world of international soccer
 Coming off the best season of his career, Ousmane Dembélé spent a defining summer in the United States, one of three host nations of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Arriving as the reigning Ballon d’Or winner, the Paris Saint-Germain star carried the weight of great expectations. For Numéro New York , Dembélé reflects on ambition and the quiet determination behind his remarkable journey from modest beginnings in Normandy to the pinnacle of international soccer.
 Words by Delphine Roche ,  
 portraits by Jean-Baptiste Mondino ,  
 styling by Charles Varenne . 
 Published on 11 November 2026. Updated on 11 November 2026.
 -->
 Ousmane Dembélé wears a double-breasted jacket, a shirt, wool and cashmere suit trousers, and derby shoes, ZEGNA. 
 The Évreux kid who became the king of soccer
 Ousmane Dembélé cultivated a notably quiet, unassuming public presence. Combined with his formidable talent, that humility has made him one of French soccer’s most admired figures. Born in Vernon in 1997 and raised in Évreux, Dembélé spent his childhood firmly rooted in Normandy. 
 He began playing at ALM Évreux before joining Évreux FC 27 , and at 13 left for the Stade Rennais F.C. academy . Évreux has since acquired a remarkable reputation as a breeding ground for French soccer talent, with internationals including Dayot Upamecano and Brice Samba also emerging from the city.

 The roots of a success story
 Having won the 2025 Ballon d’Or , the sport’s most prestigious individual accolade, a visibly moved Dembélé paid tribute to the city of his youth during his acceptance speech. His enduring attachment to the people and places that nurtured his talent points to an aspect of soccer too often obscured by its hyper-capitalist excesses: the more modest reality of local clubs and coaches, whose dedication instills in children both the joy of the game and an ethos of collective endeavor.
 “ I cherish countless memories from my childhood, particularly in Évreux, as that is where I grew up and where everything began for me ,” he reflects. “ To this day, that town remains deeply important to me. When I meet young people from the same neighborhood or a similar background who tell me they used to watch me play, it resonates profoundly. It also carries a responsibility: to demonstrate that one can achieve success while remaining authentic and honoring those who supported you along the way .”
 Ousmane Dembélé wears a grained leather shirt, a cashmere turtleneck jumper and wool cloth trousers, ZEGNA. 
 Navigating different environments growing up
 Like many of his compatriots on the national team, Dembélé was raised at the intersection of several cultures. Born into a family with roots in West Africa, he considers that heritage fundamental to his identity. “ Growing up with multiple cultures, diverse traditions and varied perspectives taught me from a very young age to be open-minded and proud of my roots ,” he notes. “ I believe it is a fundamental part of who I am today .”
 The enduring poetry of soccer lies in the fact that the stories of its multimillionaire icons so often have the same humble beginnings: a young boy kicking a ball around with neighborhood friends. Then comes the plot twist, an extraordinary talent that proves impossible to ignore.

 “ Futsal was a masterclass in technique because everything happens in a flash. With so little space, decisions must be instantaneous ,” Ousmane Dembélé
 For Dembélé , a pure love of the game drove him to hone his technique on both traditional pitches and futsal courts. The latter, in particular, sharpened his speed of execution and precision in tight spaces. “ Futsal was a masterclass in technique because everything happens in a flash ,” he recalls. “ With so little space, decisions must be instantaneous. It truly refines your first touch, dribbling, sudden changes of direction and ability with both feet. Yet, back then, I wasn’t analyzing any of it. I simply wanted to play and have fun. ”
 When Dembélé left Évreux to join Stade Rennais F.C. in neighboring Brittany, he developed into a remarkably versatile attacker, equally comfortable on either flank and capable of moving inside into more central positions. “ My attributes naturally lent themselves to the wing: pace, dribbling and one-on-one situations ,” he says. “ And being equally comfortable with both feet allowed me to operate on either side. But I never fancied being confined to a single position. I have always craved freedom on the pitch .”
 Ousmane Dembélé wears a leather zipped jacket and derby shoes, ZEGNA. Technical jersey shorts, ADIDAS. 
 “ I never fancied being confined to a single position. I have always craved freedom on the pitch ,” Ousmane Dembélé
 In October 2015, he signed his first professional contract with Rennes. The following month, he made his Ligue 1 debut against Angers. By the end of that breakthrough season, he had been named Ligue 1 Young Player of the Year .
 Following such a rapid ascent, it wasn’t long before Dembélé caught the eye of Europe’s elite. In the summer of 2016, less than a year after his Ligue 1 debut, he joined Borussia Dortmund . International recognition swiftly followed. In September that year, he made his senior debut for France. Just twelve months later, he secured a blockbuster move to FC Barcelona.

 “ Occasionally, I will isolate a single player for 30 or 40 minutes, studying his movements, his runs and his spatial awareness without the ball ,” Ousmane Dembélé
 With his meteoric rise came the unforgiving pressures of elite soccer, and his first genuine setbacks. A succession of injuries disrupted his six seasons at Barcelona, beginning with a ruptured hamstring tendon shortly after his arrival that sidelined him for more than three months. Although he was part of the France squad that won the 2018 World Cup, his role in the tournament was limited and head coach Didier Deschamps frequently left him on the bench.
 “ There were extraordinary moments in Barcelona, but also arduous periods that demanded immense patience and mental fortitude ,” Dembélé recalls. “ When you endure repeated injuries, you learn a great deal about your body and your character. Over time, I also found a way to distance myself from the external noise and focus exclusively on what I can control. ”
 Where many young prodigies might have succumbed to such adversity, gradually fading from the spotlight, Dembélé found a second wind in the eye of the storm. His resilience stems from a simple truth: an undiminished devotion to the game. “ Transitioning to the professional ranks inevitably burdens your shoulders with immense pressure ,” he says. “ But the moment you lose the joy of playing, the challenge becomes insurmountable .”
 “ I strive to preserve the exact pleasure I felt in my youth: possessing the ball, combining with teammates and attempting to create something out of nothing. I am above all a true lover of soccer. I watch an extraordinary number of matches. Occasionally, I will isolate a single player for 30 or 40 minutes, studying his movements, his runs and his spatial awareness without the ball. I essentially scan him .”
 Ousmane Dembélé wears a wool cloth coat, a double-breasted jacket and a long-sleeved wool polo shirt, ZEGNA. 
 “ Operating centrally allows me to drop deep, drive forward, combine in tight spaces or drift out wide ,” Ousmane Dembélé
 Returning to France in 2023, Dembélé rapidly established himself as a cornerstone of Paris Saint-Germain ’s new sporting philosophy. Under Luis Enrique , the club began pivoting away from its era of individualistic superstar signings, instead constructing a more sustainable, collective project built around youth, tactical cohesion and long-term stability.
 During the 2024-25 campaign, Enrique made a decisive tactical adjustment, moving Dembélé from the wing into a more central, fluid role. The shift revitalized his game, giving him greater freedom while transforming his influence on PSG’s attack.
 “ I thoroughly enjoy this newfound freedom ,” Dembélé remarks. “ Operating centrally allows me to drop deep, drive forward, combine in tight spaces or drift out wide. It demands an acute understanding with my teammates, given how frequently we rotate positions. I believe this role has cultivated a more complete version of myself and, above all, allowed me to exert a greater influence on the match .”

 “ Today, my philosophy centers entirely on the collective ,” Ousmane Dembélé
 When PSG finally lifted the long-awaited UEFA Champions League trophy in May 2025, Dembélé proved instrumental in the club’s spectacular 5-0 victory over Inter Milan. He provided two assists while contributing tirelessly to PSG’s pressing game.
 “ Today, my philosophy centers entirely on the collective ,” Dembélé explains. “ Naturally, a forward relishes scoring or assisting, but elite matches demand universal sacrifice. Winning the ball back, or executing a press that triggers a goal seconds later, holds equal merit. When you win a final of that magnitude, it’s the collective triumph that endures .”
 Taking home the 2025 Ballon d’Or appears to have done little to alter Dembélé’s grounded nature. Yet his ascent to soccer’s ultimate individual summit remains unusual. Dembélé represents a compelling counterpoint to the archetype of prolific individual stars. His brilliance lies as much in his selflessness as in his attacking gifts.
 Reflecting on his historic first-half hat trick against Norway at this summer’s World Cup , becoming the first player to achieve that feat since 1994, he remains understated. “ I feel there have been other matches where my overall influence on the pitch was far greater. Goals are important, of course, but my priority is always to elevate the team and deliver a complete performance in every facet of the game .”
 Ousmane Dembélé wears a double-breasted wool and mohair jacket, a cotton poplin tuxedo shirt, a bow tie and cufflinks, ZEGNA. 
 “ Goals are important, of course, but my priority is always to elevate the team and deliver a complete performance in every facet of the game ,” Ousmane Dembélé
 Such humility is precisely what has forged Dembélé’s profound connection with the PSG fanbase. When he arrived at the Théâtre du Châtelet for the 2025 Ballon d’Or ceremony, the chant “ Et Ousmane Ballon d’Or ! ” had followed him across Paris. Now nominated for a second consecutive Ballon d’Or following PSG’s back-to-back Champions League triumphs, Dembélé again deflects the spotlight.
 “ I don’t need to stand alone at the pinnacle to find fulfillment. I would much rather we all reach the top together ,” he notes. “ My only certainty is that the Ballon d’Or belongs in Paris this year. What we achieved last season was even more historic than our campaign the year before. ”
